values.value: How close is your audience data to something a unified profile can be built from — one identifiable person across sources, or per-campaign tables that only make sense to the campaign that built them?

[{"value":1,"label":"Per-campaign tables with no shared key. Nobody could say which rows are the same person."},{"value":2,"label":"A dominant key exists in practice, but joins are manual and each team maintains its own copy."},{"value":3,"label":"A documented model with a stable key; identity across sources is a mapping exercise, not a discovery one."},{"value":4,"label":"A unified profile already exists and is load-bearing \u2014 Data Cloud or equivalent, with identity resolution configured."}]

skills/mce-mcn-helper/references/framework-reference.md — "Subscriber Key / Contact Key -> Unified Individual (Party ID) (Replaced). Not a field rename. Identity is resolved across all sources automatically"; and "Data Extension -> Data Model Object. Discipline shifts from schema design to schema mapping." A 4 now means "identity resolution already done", which is materially harder to earn than the base anchor, because on this target it is the thing the whole Foundation phase exists to build.
